13c(ii)

The minimum kinetic energy that was calculated in part (c)(i) is converted entirely into mass to account for the mass defect. 

In order for momentum to be conserved, the reaction products (on the right-hand side of the equation) cannot be stationary after the collision, in other words, they must have some kinetic energy.

This kinetic energy comes from the kinetic energy of the neutron which means that the neutron's kinetic energy and as a result, its speed, must be larger than the minimum value calculated in part (c)(i).
